definitions.explanation: A person who robs travelers on the road, historically by stripping them of their clothing and belongings. In modern usage, can refer more generally to mugging or robbery.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{街道|かいどう}→街道：14040_kaidou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{追|お}いはぎ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: In the old days, highway robbers appeared on this road.

examples.japanese: {追|お}いはぎ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遭|あ}って→遭う：09500_au⟧{身|み}ぐるみ⟦{剥|は}がされた→剥がす：00081_hagasu⟧。
examples.english: I was robbed by a mugger and stripped of everything.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{料金|りょうきん}→料金：03797_ryoukin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{追|お}いはぎ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ようなものだ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{文句|もんく}→文句：03636_monku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}った→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: He complained that the charge was highway robbery.

notes:
From {追|お}い{剥|は}ぎ — literally "chasing and stripping." Originally referred to bandits on roads who would waylay travelers and strip them of their clothing and possessions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {追|お}いはぎ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遭|あ}う→遭う：09500_au⟧: to be robbed by a mugger
- {追|お}いはぎ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: highway robbers appear
- {追|お}いはぎ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような: like highway robbery (figurative)

USAGE:
In modern Japanese, often used figuratively to describe exorbitant prices or charges, similar to the English expression "highway robbery." For example, {追|お}いはぎ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{値段|ねだん}→値段：00871_nedan⟧ (highway-robbery prices).

ETYMOLOGY:
During the Edo period, {追|お}いはぎ were a real danger on the roads between cities. They feature prominently in historical fiction and period dramas (⟦{時代劇|じだいげき}→時代劇：12968_jidaigeki⟧).
